title: Define strict CCP2 corpus and consumer contract
description:
Scope: revision-specific fixture/schema entries in /home/mark/Developer/lichen-workspace/project-LICHEN/test/vectors/ and their existing registration in /home/mark/Developer/lichen-workspace/project-LICHEN/python/tests/test_vectors.py. Define closed, bounded case families, unique IDs, requirement references, oracle provenance, source/wire/corpus revisions, and an explicit nonempty applicability inventory. Specify the language-neutral consumer input, operation, expected outcome and case-accounting contract without implementing production adapters. Reuse existing schema validation rather than mandating a new framework or file layout.

HPC8 execution policy: Code, test, or schema changes require three independent correctness, security, and robustness reviews; file and fix all findings and re-review. Use independent oracles, never weakened legacy tests or self-generated expected results. Preserve upstream Yggdrasil addressing, radio-owned identity, best-effort custody, baseline SCHC, and the human-only OSCORE/EDHOC security edit bar. External actions, hardware/RF operations, and port access require scoped explicit permission and applicable bench safety checks. Research may conclude no-go; an authorization gate requires affirmative, recorded approval for its actual scope. Dependency closure and decomposition are not permission. No speculative activation, including deferred portability or experimental modes.
design: Use the existing per-family or shared-schema pattern that best fits. Keep fixture format_version independent of policy/wire versions, and define a finite inventory that later consumers must report exactly.
acceptance_criteria: The vector tree has an explicit strict schema policy for every CCP2 family and the corpus manifest/consumer contract is self-contained. Independent malformed-document tests reject unknown kinds, missing families, duplicate IDs, wrong versions, bool-as-integer inputs and empty selections. No new CCP2 family is added to the pending-schema exemption list. Every required consumer operation has typed inputs and an expected observable outcome; no production API or on-air configuration is enabled.
